refuter_findings.location: ## Statement, displayed estimate with C e^{Ct}; SI interpretation in Remarks
refuter_findings.evidence: The fixed-gauge definition says the time parameter is x^0 in metres and the normalized state norm is dimensionless. In the homogeneous estimate, the leading C must therefore be dimensionless, while C in e^{Ct} must have units m^{-1}. The same constant cannot have both units; the stated SI interpretation needs separate constants or dimensionless time.

refuter_findings.location: ## Statement, paragraph beginning “Fix a compact parameter interval”
refuter_findings.evidence: The Statement requires K to be a compact subset of the “position-velocity phase space” without defining that space or its domain. The cited coordinate geodesic equation supplier gives the geodesic ODE in chart coordinates but does not define this phase space. Specify, for example, TU={(p,v):p∈U, v∈T_pM}, so K's membership and compactness have an exact domain.

refuter_findings.location: ## Statement, sentence stating both proper times are ℓ/c
refuter_findings.evidence: The Statement assigns x^0 and ℓ units of metres but states only c>0. The proper-time definition says it fixes no physical dimension for c and defers that reading to the SI convention, which gives c units m s^{-1} and proper time in seconds. The example does not state that convention, so its SI interpretation of ℓ/c as a duration is under-specified.
